reviews.text: An excellent, embodied turn from Olivia Colman is no huge surprise these days, but she is particularly magnetic here, in a part that leaves room for interpretation.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: To some regret, the first act of the film is drawn out exposition with no real insight as to where the plot could be headed. However, when it does find its rhythm, it is almost addictive in a way.
reviews.author: Yasmine Kandil

reviews.text: “The Lost Daughter” is one of the best films in 2021 because it shows us a story of an imperfect, often annoying and reckless protagonist, but makes viewers get invested in her story even when she commits unlikable acts.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: If one is willing to make the effort to embrace the fractured nature of the protagonist, The Lost Daughter is a puzzle that, although not entirely solvable, is rich in its complexities.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: A triumphant directorial debut by Maggie Gyllenhaal, The Lost Daughter shouts volumes of emotions while crisscrossing between the choices Leda made in her past and similar situations on her vacation in the present.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter isn’t necessarily a celebration of a complicated woman, but it is a searingly honest portrayal. This look at motherhood isn’t intended to be perfect. It’s much more interested in all of the ugliness that’s involved.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Colman delivers a performance filled with heartbreak and anger, and one that also shows the vulnerable aspect of Leda’s motherhood.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: The directorial debut from accomplished actress Maggie Gyllenhaal is a stunning sign of (hopefully) more great projects to come.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: "The film is brilliant at parsing the dual sin of reluctant motherhood. In The Lost Daughter, love is not unconditional, but it doesn’t mean it isn’t there."
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: A drama with a heightened psychological edge, The Lost Daughter, is an absorbing and unsettling depiction of motherhood with standout performances from Olivia Coleman and Jesse Buckley.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is a mesmerizing meditation on the messiness of motherhood - and a distinguished debut for Maggie Gyllenhaal as a writer and director - led by a career-best Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Watching [Colman] ascend to the heights of being an esteemed, lauded actress over the past few years has been thrilling, and in this film, she may just deliver her best performance to date.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: For any director, this is audacious and intricate terrain, but Gyllenhaal is as exceptional and daring a filmmaker as she is a performer.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal hits all the right chords in this finespun story where the past rushes over the present. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Weaves the ins and outs of motherhood through the psychology of a complex character full of contradictions, played by a wonderful Olivia Colman. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carla Monfort

reviews.text:
Provokes indifference rather than intrigue.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: There is an exaggerated underlining of these images that at times makes them lose their freshness a bit, almost as if we have Maggie Gyllenhal pinching us on the shoulder and saying See? Did you understand? There!
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: Through flashbacks, Gyllenhaal makes the bizarre or mysterious elements of the film too clear, right up to the end.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: A subtly devastating psychological drama which marks a significant directorial debut for well-known actor Maggie Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Its rare to find a debut film as confident as The Lost Daughter. In Gyllenhaal, there is a new director who has a clear idea of the type of stories she wants to tell. I can only hope she gets to tell more in the future.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Its a ludicrous proposition offered by Gyllenhaal, to hang out with these people, but it makes for a terrifyingly artful film about bad parenting.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: This is a quiet, thoughtful film about imperfect people, hinting at an imperfect truth.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: In broadcasting an unpopular, and rarely-voiced truth about maternal instincts, the movie ruffles feathers even as it offers comfort, a most prickly sort of solace.
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter peels back the poetic idea of a mother’s unconditional love, revealing prosaic truths and harsh realities we often shy from.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal makes a shattering debut as a writer and director in The Lost Daughter, a quietly intense drama about a woman on vacation who learns the old lesson that no matter where you go, there you are.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Did I love this movie? No, but its message and performances are liberating. Take or leave what Gyllenhaal and Ferrante are selling, but some respect and attention are in order.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Olivia Colman delivers an outstanding performance in this evocative and unconventional psychological drama that explores the complex meaning of motherhood. Full Review in Spanish
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is a difficult film to process, but it's all the richer for it. Gyllenhaal displays fresh talent behind the camera in her feature directorial debut
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: A raw & compelling take on the "crushing responsibility" of motherhood a perspective that's rarely shown in such bold strokes. It dares to question, but never judge, the value of motherhood for a character who finds that parenting doesn't come naturally.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: Colman is marvelous... Jessie Buckley is terrific... The film is a noble first effort from the talented actress-turned-director.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Kudos to The Lost Daughter for closing 2021 out with one last thought-provoking, immaculately crafted piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Like the beach Leda frequents, The Lost Daughter offers up an unsettling aura to languish in and plenty of characters to try and decode.
reviews.author: Steph Green

reviews.text: the romance of the setting is undermined by the harshness of the human behaviour it places under the microscope...
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Colman can make Leda simply driving a car seem dramatic, as the expression on her face quietly captures the emotional turmoil she tries so hard to contain. And Gyllenhaal can turn an image of rotting fruit into a jump-scare.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Overall a stirring screen adaptation with superb performance.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: A psychological drama that deals with motherhood, depression, and life choices.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Even if it has the ability to frustrate, it's an accomplished film, which has the courage to assert - against the grain of traditional Hollywood movies - that motherhood may not be for every woman.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: ...offers quite a lot worth discovering, a thoughtful (and sometimes devastating) inquiry into a woman's desires, ambitions, doubts and regrets.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's portrait of an anti-holiday filled with minor annoyances mirrors the intimate, self-conscious and at times unsettling nature of Ferrante's novel.
reviews.author: Rebecca Liu

reviews.text: The character Leda calls to mind is The Wolf of Wall Street's Jordan Belfort.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal has a promising debut as a director as we can easily see the kinds of stories and characters she wants to tackle.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The film is a harsh illumination of a woman's life, a story about remorse whose evocation of an almost cosmic sense of fate and providence might make some viewers catch their breath with a surprised shock of recognition.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: No likable characters exist in this dull, feel-bad film of the decade.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Well acted and directed but it is a depressing movie overall.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Colman is quietly impressive in a nuance-rich portrait...Yet, the film's pace does wilt and the wavering story doesn't totally pay off, leaving us with a decidedly "meh" finale. Gyllenhaal keeps things on simmer when she could have turned up the heat.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: When mothers, fathers, husbands, and wives ditch commitments in search of the true self, it's a move that fails to satisfy. It's an escape but not a solution.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: It is possible to admire a film like The Lost Daughter - the meticulous vision, the earnest performances, the profound themes - and not like it very much.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: achieves little more than tedium because it is anchored to such an impenetrable, disagreeable character whose every action is little more than a meandering dead end
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: In her feature debut, Gyllenhaal slowly paints an emotional yet intimate portrait that questions the rigidly established structures of motherhood, with fairly organic performances by Olivia Colman and Jessie Buckley. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter conveys, in a way films rarely do, the intimacy, the intensity, the immensity of caring for small children, of being their whole world.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Colman is one of the very best actors now working. By the end, she makes you understand this complicated character.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: A picture that is both simpler and more profound than you imagined.
reviews.author: Tori Preston

reviews.text: Depending on how you want to look at it, this could be the best Mother's Day movie ever or the worst.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is one of the best films of 2021 and should earn deserved Oscar nominations for its star, Olivia Colman, and for Jessie Buckley, superbly cast as Colman's younger self.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: All of the symbolism and subtext about the expectation of women as mothers and the ugly belief that women who do not have children are making a mistake rises to the fore. This is, in fact, a potent cinematic exploration of women and motherhood.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is about the tussle between motherhood and agency, seeing the two as mutually exclusive, feeling utterly trapped by the role that's expected to come naturally to you.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: A bold and defiant feature film debut that tackles a taboo subject rarely depicted on screen. It's a slow but ultimately rewarding experience, featuring a trifecta of terrific performances from Colman, Johnson + Buckley.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter uses subtlety to bring about specific emotions that not everyone will be able to relate to, but the impact is there.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: This is a fine, unsettling film about the cost of the choices we make.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: There's something refreshing, exciting and endlessly engaging about The Lost Daughter's ability to make us care so much about a person who's donned prickly, spiked armor to keep everyone else away.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is an extraordinary drama. It grabs you and won't let go.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It addresses the impossible, ordinary, maddening task of keeping both yourself and a child alive.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: The end is deeply ambiguous, neither punishing nor condoning its characters' behavior. It simply asks us to sit with them - to pay them the respect of attention, and learn something about ourselves in the process.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It is phenomenally filmed by Maggie Gyllenhaal and acted with great ferocity by Olivia Colman and Jessie Buckley.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: Another fantastic performance by Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: As its story plays out, you can't help but be drawn in closer by the work of Colman and Buckley. Two actors portraying different stages of the same person's life is nothing new to cinema. Rarely has it been done this seamlessly.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: This anxiety-triggering psychological thriller covers the side of parenting no one talks about.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Though the story is Ferrante's, Gyllenhaal has already been richly rewarded for a script that requires no grandiose budget, and a film that relies primarily on a sharp eye and willingness to go where no one else dares to.
reviews.author: Toba Singer

reviews.text: With a great central performance from Olivia Colman, it has depth, intelligence and a powerful seriousness of purpose. It's also unfailingly grim, which raises questions about how we respond, as an audience.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: It is self-assured storytelling, buoyed by wonderful performances from Coleman, Johnson and Buckley, who bring intelligence and, most importantly, humanity to characters who are not always likeable.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Coleman gives a finely calibrated performance, sly and intelligent throughout.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Leda doesn't understand her own behavior, but the viewers need to -- and the symbolism is cloudier without the clearer context provided by Elena Ferrante's source novel. Daughters, mothers, daughters, husbands, sons -- we're all left a little lost.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: A film that depicts motherhood from a place rarely seen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: This is what people mean when they say they want to go out and see a film.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: In fact, the piece can be slow enough in spots to cause you to question where Gyllenhaal is taking you, but this is a film you shouldn't fully judge until its final moments.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: A dark, brooding tale of motherhood viewed without sentiment, and with a sensibility that makes it feel curiously foreign despite being in English... Whether it's more probing or mystifying is a matter of debate.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Whatever the conventions and shortcuts of literary adaptation that the movie reflects, Gyllenhaal has thrown down a gauntlet to filmmakers and producers, to the movie industry at large, and to the future of the art.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: The beauty of the film is just how genuine and down-to-earth the performances are and how Gyllenhaal maintains this natural authentic tone throughout the film.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Jessie Buckley, Dakota Johnson and Peter Sarsgaard round out a stellar cast.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: It's worth seeing, but it is an intellectual movie. But the biggest reason to see it is for Olivia Colman's performance.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Although not much happens during the course of The Lost Daughter, the film's tone exerts a powerful spell.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: No one says what they mean in Maggie Gyllenhaal's astonishing directorial debut The Lost Daughter, but everything they do say is loaded with meaning.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: In her premiere efforts as a writer/director, Gyllenhaal nails it. Not only is it a phenomenal psychological drama, but a monumental accomplishment.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Despite the uneven and questionable ending, this is a deep and abiding inspection of motherhood, deemed to be perfect by society but flawed through imperfect human beings.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Pandemic fatigue cinema rules the awards with sympathetic portrayals of repugnant self-hating protagonists, fear or mockery of the 'other' disgruntled masses rising up on the left and right, and film world dread in the downward spiraling low wage economy.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter" is a solid debut from Maggie Gyllenhaal even if the disjoined narrative occasionally creates a jarring viewing experience.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter, a sharply crafted, clear-eyed interrogation of less-than-likable parents, ebbs and flows on the strength of this reality, along with a few immense performers from its veteran ensemble.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter" certainly raises as many questions as it answers, which is why it is so gratifying.... Gyllenhaal's film is mysterious too. It sinks its hooks into viewers and does not let go.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: An intimate and honest portrait of the challenges and psychological pressures that society imposes on motherhood. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is a first-time director with a voice-someone who can conjure up suspense from an unbroken shot of an orange being peeled.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: An impressive debut feature for Gyllenhaal, showcasing an intelligence and empathy that I suspect will only strengthen as her career continues.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's directorial debut is a gripping drama about parental strife.
reviews.author: Jon Winkler

reviews.text: A sobering drama about how motherhood can sometimes bring out our shadow sides.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter marks acclaimed actress Maggie Gyllenhaal's debut as a writer and director. But the psychological drama unfolds in such a confident and mesmerising fashion that you wouldn't know it.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: It's an auspicious debut from Gyllenhaal, who observes every little moment with intense focus, and another riveting performance from Colman, who develops a wrenching portrait of motherhood with quiet, chilling intensity.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is a triumph of adaptation for writer and first-time feature director Maggie Gyllenhaal. Her film, relocating the novel's southern Italian setting to a Greek island, spins a subtle web of intrigue. "Subtle," however, doesn't mean calm.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Equal parts troubling and affecting, Leda epitomizes a type of woman whose needs are rarely addressed in American mainstream movies. We can dislike her, but we are never permitted to revile her.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is tough-minded in its emotional approach but Gyllenhaal directs with tenderness and curiosity. She has made a movie that asks a lot of compelling questions, with the biggie being, "Isn't motherhood hard?"
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter isn't unconfident in its depiction, nor vague in its thematic expression, which places Gyllenhaal out ahead of most of her Hollywood contemporaries at least.
reviews.author: M.G. Mailloux

reviews.text: Let's just cut to the chase. The Lost Daughter is the don't-miss movie of 2021.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: It is the filmmaker's deft grasp of the dynamics between women, not just mothers and daughters, that makes the film compelling.
reviews.author: Caitlin Quinlan

reviews.text: You wonder where this film is going, but Colman's performance is so subtle, yet telling and often terribly disturbing seeing her past as well as present laid out by Director Gyllenhaal with such intricate detail.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The film is imperfect and obstinate, and in that is just what makes it so effective as high art. Gyllenhal is a filmmaking voice to watch.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Colman shines at the forefront of the movie, although her character makes odd decisions that will have most mothers thinking about their own relationships with their children.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter bucks conventions to become one of the few films of 2021 that is simply impossible to forget.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal leans toward the thriller genre, which disguises what is essentially a lo-fi drama.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Colman brings Ferrante's creation to life with all the withering pathos she deserves. Gyllenhaal catches it handsomely, awe-struck, as if even she didn't know how painfully real this woman Leda could seem or, in Colman's hands, be.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: With brilliant work by Olivia Colman, Maggie Gyllenhaal's directing debut is a haunting work about choices, motherhood, and memory.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: A powerful and compelling drama about a woman haunted by the "crushing responsibility of motherhood" and the things you aren't allowed to say out loud.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Thank Maggie Gyllenhaal, in a stunning debut as director and screenwriter, for creating one of the year's very best movies starring the magnificent Olivia Colman as a mother haunted by her troubled past. This, you do not want to miss.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Olivia Colman is one of the best actresses in the world, and has been for quite some time.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: It's quite a high-wire act [director Maggie Gyllenhaal] achieves here.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Prepare for it to work its subtle magic, wow you with its tender performances, and hurt and heal you with its moving, discomforting truths about mothers and daughters and the women struggling to be both.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter expertly and fearlessly deconstructs motherhood as an institution and marks Maggie Gyllenhaal as a director and screenwriter to watch.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: It's the kind of movie that haunts you for a while afterward, like clouds that hang in the sky long after the storm has passed.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter" is a harsh and uncompromising film. It has a mean streak that I found impactful.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It rummages around beneath the surface so ruthlessly, that it can't help but open our eyes. And our hearts.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It's a moviegoing experience, sure - and if you need to hear it, one of the best of the year. But it's really a call to compassion, which makes it transcendent.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is a grueling yet ultimately rewarding ride, giving viewers an opportunity to shift their own views on the characters on multiple occasions.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: There is perhaps no relationship more fraught than that between a mother and her daughter, and in The Lost Daughter that tension becomes so brittle it snaps.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: Savage, sophisticated, and sensual, The Lost Daughter is a psychological thriller that will titillate and terrify, then leave you stranded to pick up the tattered pieces.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: In Maggie Gyllenhaal's often unsettling adaptation of Elena Ferrante's novel, she crafts a portrait of mothers at the end of their wits that is perceptive and relatable and fearless.
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: Director Maggie Gyllenhaal gives us a fresh take on the inner workings of women, and with Leda gives us a complex female protagonist that stridently defies what we usually see explored.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: We fail ourselves first, Leda might say, but language rarely does. Neither will this film, which, like a great poem, should stand the test of time
reviews.author: Chuck Wilson

reviews.text: The longer the picture holds back answers, the greater the chance of losing viewers; some of the scenarios are intriguing, but most threaten to bore.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: While Gyllenhaal's direction is assured, the film's absorbing start sadly gives way to an ambling second hour that deprives it of enduring impact.
reviews.author: Max Copeman

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal does an impressive job of telling a complex story with few words but heaps of atmosphere and tension. Disturbing but highly effective.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter upends the stereotype that mothers depicted in movies are supposed to think that parenthood is the greatest thing that ever happened to them ... Olivia Colman anchors the movie with a memorable and intriguing performance.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Anyone who has ever heard a baby cry unattended in a supermarket will find Gyllenhaal's film an uncomfortable watch, in its presentation and validation of "bad" motherhood as transgressive liberation from society's mores.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal's feature debut as writer-director is an impressively atmospheric piece of work - filled with longing and dread, and heavy with the anticipation of buried secrets about to be revealed.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal, in her directorial debut, and leading actress Colman tell a story layered with a thousand daily tragedies, the menace of the mundane, and the pitfalls of the past.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is a stark, unapologetic look at the cost of mothering, and Olivia Colman, Dakota Johnson, and Jessie Buckley give ferociously compelling performances.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: One of the year's very best movies - a spookily complex character study of a woman who's either a terrible mother or who can't forgive herself for not being a better one.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A crushing, honest drama about the cruelties of motherhood.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Count me among those who consider Olivia Colman indispensable.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is one of those close-minded Hollywood liberals who confuse self-pity with political enmity.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: As far as directorial kickoffs go, this one is a stunner.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Following two other fine behind-camera debuts by actresses Rebecca Hall ("Passing") and Justine Bateman ("Violet"), Maggie Gyllenhaal wears director and writer hats well, too, in piling layers and layers of understanding into her novel-based dandy.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Galvanized by another quietly powerful performance from Olivia Colman, this richly textured drama marks a sharp directorial debut for actor Maggie Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal makes an intriguing directorial debut, brilliantly casting Olivia Colman as a sort of arthouse Larry David.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's freshman courage in sitting with discomfort is why the film succeeds.
reviews.author: Kimberly Reyes

reviews.text: With her impressive directing debut here, I can't decide if I want to see Gyllenhaal in front of or behind the camera, but I look forward to whatever she chooses.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal herself is a thoughtful and complex actress. So, it's unsurprising that she pulls and captures such layered performances from her core trio of actresses.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Olivia Colman makes even the most pedestrian emotions seem poetic.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter is a profound cinematic triumph. Director/WriterMaggie Gylllenhaal and her master class of actors create an intricate, mesmerizing and unnerving film experience. Not to be missed!
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: An original character study that spirals like a thriller, The Lost Daughter is an exhilarating, unsparing examination of modern motherhood -- its joys and discontents.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: [A] smart, thought-provoking adaptation of Elena Ferrante's novel.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: It's one of the very best films of the year, establishing Colman as one of our greatest actresses, Buckley as one of our greatest younger ones, and Gyllenhaal as an incredibly talented and intuitive filmmaker.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: You'd think it was unfilmable, particularly as the central character describes herself as someone even she doesn't understand but, directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal and starring Olivia Colman, this film is entirely gripping. No ambivalence on that count.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: It's ambitious and fascinating.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: What a debut it is. Harrowing, unpredictable, painful, confrontational, this is a movie for grown-ups.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal balances the here and now with the then and there pretty perfectly, showing how a past experience can influence our current decisions in ways that might seem irrational even to ourselves.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal steps behind the camera and hits a home run...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: There's a lot to take in on this multi-layered story and the characters are often unlikeable, but it's so lively and troubling that you just can't look away.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: I haven't read Ferrante's novel but I can imagine all this being skilfully rendered in prose and not quite working on screen. Yet it does work, projecting a vivid sense of unease.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal and Colman work together beautifully, the first-time director's unfussy camera ceding the actress room to hint at Leda's roiling emotions.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: [Gyllenhaal's] direction is unemphatic without ever being tentative, and she's made a film with a relaxed, easy rhythm - but not too easy.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: This is a film all about personal space, closeness and intrusion - and though there is little overt violence the threat of danger seems to be everywhere for Leda, not least the danger of her own thoughts.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter isn't just cleverly adapted, it is also a film that knows its audience and trusts them to understand the original text's motives. Maggie Gyllenhaal
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal has achieved quite the debut...her entire cast is exemplary and her writing is superb.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal keeps things compelling as we wonder if and how Leda will reconcile her past. A psychological drama with superb acting.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter serves as a haunting study of this character...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter" a sympathetic and sensitive directing debut for actress Maggie Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: This discomfiting but very accomplished drama, beautifully acted by all, announces Maggie Gyllenhaal not just as a capable director, but one equipped to render notably difficult, delicate, potentially off-putting material accessibly involving.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Ms. Gyllenhaal might have chosen conventionally entertaining material for her first time behind the camera, but she and Ms. Colman turn The Lost Daughter into something memorable.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal approaches the story boldly, with vision, but her film sometimes feels over-directed, and while Colman is a wonderful actress, her talent is lent on a little too heavily here.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal keeps us on edge right until the end. But her true gift is in the way she trusts her actors and allowing Colman and Buckley's performances perfectly echo each other.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: It's not at all surprising that Gyllenhaal has arrived as a filmmaker with such a bold, conflicted paean to unorthodox femininity. But it's thrilling just the same.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: We've seen good moms, bad moms, crazy moms, selfish moms, generous moms, loving moms, cold moms. But what strikes home so vividly in The Lost Daughter... is how rarely we see a mother who is all those things at once.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter, and the 2006 Elena Ferrante novel on which it is scrupulously based, is a beach read in the literal sense.
reviews.author: Stephen Elliott

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter does well to blend its dramatic, thrilling, and darkly comedic tones together for something profound.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Colman and Buckley's performances elevated what I thought wasn't always particularly interesting material.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The atmosphere, performances, and patient revelations are so precisely managed by its writer-director, Maggie Gyllenhaal, that it's hard to believe this is her debut behind the camera.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is the type of story that separates guilt from regret to expose how Leda possesses none of the former. She owns her tears, unapologetically.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Colman is superb in the lead, a guarded woman running warm and cool, used to keeping her emotions hidden until she recognizes the same marital and maternal discontent she once experienced herself in another.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal isn't interested in judgment, only truth. Every decision she makes is exactly the right one.
reviews.author: Johanna Schneller

reviews.text: "The Lost Daughter" is a chilling and unnerving psychological horror film brimming with dicey characters who are capable of deeply disturbing behavior.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Colman's performance is coiled and complicated as a woman trying to navigate her own feelings about motherhood, and engaging in dangerous, sometimes malicious projection.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Arich, complex and fascinating performance from Olivia Colman is what gives this movie its piercing power: she has some old-school star quality and screen presence.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal makes a quietly astonishing directorial debut with "The Lost Daughter," a crafty treatise on maternal ambivalence that delivers an unsettling emotional wallop.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: A powerful, tour-de-force portrayal of the conflicts of parenting, with intimacy, intensity and a sense of tightly wound nuance.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The film is like a chase picture, with a heroine racing in vain to escape societal expectations.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal's... assured film debut as a director and writer presents an unflinching, warts-and-all portrayal of motherhood, pinned on the majesty of Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Fans of the evocative storytelling abilities of Elena Ferrante should definitely check out this hauntingly terrific adaptation of her 2008 novel The Lost Daughter.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It's a tremendous accomplishment.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Extraordinary direction, paired with exceptional performances...culminate in a perfect storm that yields an astute portrait of the painful expectations of womanhood.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: Olivia Colman portrays a complicated woman on vacation in Greece whose collision with an unpleasant family brings back memories of her own marriage and ambivalence toward motherhood.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: [A] bold, sharp-cornered film - one as admirably un-eager to please as the woman it portrays.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: The physical similarities and remarkable wavelength between Olivia Colman and Jessie Buckley are worth watching for alone. It poses challenging thoughts about motherhood and presents these controversial choices without judgment
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal gets a little tripped up while trying to compact the book into a movie, but her instincts with casting and emotional wreckage are spot-on, creating a disturbing picture that sneaks up on viewers.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It's an outstanding debut for someone who obviously knows her way around both sides of the camera.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal takes a non-judgmental approach to this rarely explored subject, but frequently frames Colman in skin-crawling close-ups that make it difficult to watch but impossible to avert your eyes.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal's directing debut is subversive yet compassionate.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: What could have been little more than an acting showcase for a reliable ensemble fully sings: a sophisticated, seductive, slightly unwieldy and often very sad study of the instability and upsets of motherhood.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: Thanks to some fine performances, and writer-director Maggie Gyllenhaal, this movie avoids the excesses that typically plague this kind of artistic drama. Instead of desperate dramatics, we get a solid story, great acting, and honest emotions.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A draining, sedate observation of material ambivalence that's sustained by a trio of knockout lead performances.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Colman can register a tumultuous inner life without any words at all...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The movie is never great, but it's never exactly dull. There's always a reason to stick around for the next scene.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: I never wrapped my head around the story - probably because I am a guy. (We are not too bright when it comes to nuance.)
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: For a while, Olivia Colman's expressive performance carries the film, with little narrative distraction or stylistic conspicuousness.
reviews.author: Diego Semerene

reviews.text: The performance by Olivia Colman is lyrical and striking.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: People are strange, complex beasts, and that's something thoroughly embraced by The Lost Daughter.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal showcases directorial chops far beyond what you'd expect for her first time out, even if she bites off more than she can chew as a screenwriter.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal has created an admiral debut and shows a very keen eye for framing.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: Nuanced, thoughtful, and deeply effective, Gyllenhaal's movie is assuredly executed, uplifted by a strong, striking performance by Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal's The Lost Daughter is a brave look at motherhood and womanhood. Colman is enchanting in one of her career best roles and Johnson's enigmatic performance is pitch perfect.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: The film's story is a slow burner with a lot of build-up but next to no payoff, with its final vague moments making the rest of the movie feel like something of a waste.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The Lost Daughter is an achingly sad directorial debut from Maggie Gyllenhaal that serves to showcase the myriad talents of star Olivia Colman.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: Strays too far from Italy to be convincing, but a stunningly good Olivia Colman saves the day.
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal has forged a powerful new myth. She and her whole team are legends.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A film about motherhood that gets right to the heart of its middle-aged protagonist, highlighting her many contradictions and flaws, alongside her sparkling charm, intellect and kindness.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: An ambitious directorial debut from Gyllenhaal...its overlong runtime and uneven supporting performances cause its dramatic effect to falter for the sake of style.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: It's a tribute to the extraordinary gifts Colman has with knowing exactly how to play to the camera. This might be her greatest film work yet.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: There isn't much in The Lost Daughter that I anticipated.. Everyone is a bundle of contradictions, a collection of venial sins, and sometimes even an example of better angels, which, in the end, are the strangest presenting phenomena of them all.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: In a movie not unlike her character on the Deuce, Maggie Gyllenhaal has purposefully and successfully moved behind the camera.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Ferrante's novels, fiercely beloved by women all over the world, have always invited ecranization, and Colman will almost certainly be a hotly-tipped award's candidate as the complex, neurotic and pensive Leda.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal masterfully milks every moment for both intrigue and insight.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal's directorial debut is a bold but flawed take on where motherhood and ambition clash.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal demonstrates impressive control for a debut director, instantly reassuring the viewer that she knows what she's doing. But she drops the ball at the end of this quietly heart-breaking drama, with the final 20 minutes begging to be cut.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: This might be one of the stronger directorial debuts--at least the most confident and forceful--by a known actress since Sarah Polley's Away From Her.
reviews.author: David Katz

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal... makes an impressive debut as both writer and director.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Buckley is terrific, her performance meshing so perfectly with Colman's that it's easy to see the older woman within the younger one, and vice-versa.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal's eye is extraordinarily perceptive, the camera almost indecently intimate in its attention to the heady sensuality of frustrated desire.
reviews.author: Anahit Behrooz

reviews.text: A hugely confident debut from a director to watch, buttressed by a screen talent performing at her peak.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It may not all add up but this is an ambitious and taboo-tackling first feature with an atmosphere that lingers thanks to gutsy performances from Colman and Buckley.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: The suspense is that of an orange being peeled in a long strip that seems like it must break at any moment.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal is gentle when needed and blunt when required, but her eye captures every emotion and element in the moment.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: It's a worthy adaptation - murkily funny, shiveringly intimate drama...
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal... keeps proving herself an artist pushing towards the edge in search of truths, no matter how uncomfortable they may be to confront.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Gyllenhaal devises a visual language that's as capricious as it is arresting. She knows exactly what she wants to capture and how, and we can feel it in the pacing and framing.
reviews.author: Cassie da Costa

reviews.text: I'm not convinced, on balance, that Gyllenhaal's delicious drama is finally much more than a storm in a teacup. But what a cup, what a storm.
reviews.author: Xan Brooks

reviews.text: Through it all, Gyllenhaal assumes an unfussy, practically invisible non-style that conveys the essential while privileging the performances.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Its strong cast and the story's granular psychological texture will make it a must-see, while putting Gyllenhaal on the map as a neophyte writer-director already graced with maturity and restraint.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Marks a supremely confident feature directing debut from Maggie Gyllenhaal, who also penned the screenplay.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Maggie Gyllenhaal puts forth something profound, specific, and even bone-deep about womanhood, motherhood, and all the unspoken horrors and repressed regrets that surround these identities.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: By empowering its female characters with ruthless honesty, the film also leaves room for self-doubt - a feature of authenticity which could potentially make up for the plot's unevenness.
reviews.author: Savina Petkova

reviews.text: Colman expertly conveys the complex intersections of Leda's actions, which out of context might seem insane. Condensed into a handful of interactions, her strength and insecurities make for an exhausting experience.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

synopsis: Alone on a seaside vacation, Leda becomes consumed with a young mother and daughter as she watches them on the beach. Unnerved by their compelling relationship, (and their raucous and menacing extended family), Leda is overwhelmed by her own memories of the terror, confusion and intensity of early motherhood. An impulsive act shocks Leda into the strange and ominous world of her own mind, where she is forced to face the unconventional choices she made as a young mother and their consequences.
